answer: Parsed 159 high-water marks (Hurricane Ida, 1 Sep 2021, NYC; USGS event 312) into hwm_clean.csv: one row per mark, columns id (hwm_id), latitude, longitude, elev_ft_navd88, height_above_gnd_ft, site (siteDescription), plus site_no, county, type, quality, uncertainty_ft. Row 1 of the raw CSV is a citation, so the header is row 2. All 159 hwm_id values are unique and all coordinates are numeric and lie within NYC. Elevations are feet NAVD88 (4.2 to 240.7, median 30.6). Height above ground is blank for 7 marks and 0 for 11; the rest run 0.3 to 6.51 ft (median about 1.5). The marks sit at 83 sites, so site is not a unique key.
traps_or_caveats: Line 1 of the CSV is a citation string, not the header; a naive read gives wrong columns. Header is on line 2.
elev_ft is surveyed water-surface elevation in feet NAVD88, NOT depth. Depth is height_above_gnd (feet above ground); do not mix them or compare to metres.
height_above_gnd is blank for 7 marks (41625, 41100, 41102, 41148, 41101, 41623, 41152), 6 of them Poor/low-quality, and 0 for 11 marks. Left as null, not filled; blank is not zero.

Marks are not independent sites: 83 sites hold 159 marks (HWM-1, HWM-2, ...). Three pairs of marks share identical coordinates (40988/41592, 40981/41310, 41146/41587). Dedupe by hwm_id, not by site or location.
Horizontal accuracy is low: all coordinates are 'WGS84 (from Digital Map)' via phone/car GPS, so positions are approximate.
5 marks have elevation from LiDAR or levelling rather than GNSS (verticalMethodName 'Other'), e.g. 41679, 41680, 41430, 41433, 41678.

Max elev 240.7 ft (hwm 40995, Staten Island, Poor quality, 0 ft above ground, near Ohrbach Lake) is a high-ground stream debris line, not NYC street flooding; treat as an outlier for elevation-based work.
Uncertainty ranges from 0.05 to 0.40 ft by quality class; the uncertainty column is only 0.1 to 0.5, and total uncertainty also includes flagging error.

hwm_environment is 'Riverine' for all marks and waterbody is mostly 'Flash flooding' (157), Harlem River (2). Marks are a surveyed sample of the event, not a complete flood extent, and are absent where no evidence was found.
The CSV is 'Filtered' by USGS; selection criteria are not documented in the files I used, so completeness is unknown. Not verified against any independent source.
Data dictionary has a mis-encoded character (O?Connor) in the reference; harmless.
